_about: Region registry for the globe. Coordinates copied from pieces/01-seafloor/viewer/live_core.js LIVE_SPOTS. type: beach|hurricane|tornado|storm; status: unlocked|forecast-only|locked. link opens the seafloor viewer on the named LAYERS label (?layer=).

regions.name: Porto Batel / Consolação
regions.layer: Reef maps: Consolação and Porto Batel
regions.note: Peniche, Portugal. 2011 lidar reef map; Consolação shares the map, 1 km away.

regions.name: Hossegor / La Gravière
regions.layer: Reef map: Hossegor / La Gravière, France

regions.name: Klitmøller
regions.note: Marked spot, no model yet: no reef-scale seabed yet.

wanted.needs: A seabed depth survey of the Klitmøller reef at 10 m resolution or finer.

regions.name: Hvide Sande
regions.note: Marked spot, no model yet: moving sandbars, no reef-scale seabed.

wanted.needs: A recent seabed depth survey of the Hvide Sande sandbars at 10 m resolution or finer.

regions.name: Tel Aviv
regions.note: Marked spot, no model yet: no seabed map yet.

wanted.needs: A seabed depth survey of the Tel Aviv surf zone at 10 m resolution or finer.

wantedSpots._about: Extra wanted markers read by globe.js from the research file (not copied here, so the research stays the one source). kind wave/research: WANTED card; kind hazard: calm 'DATA NEEDED' card. quickUnlock: ids whose known_data names an open grid at about 10 m or finer that covers the spot (picked by hand 2026-11-22; coverage stated as unconfirmed, profile lines only or licence unknown were left out). skipIfLowConfidence: ids hidden while their confidence is low.

cards._about: Round 4: finished card text for research cards that read as working notes. Written only from the entry's own fields in research/wanted-spots.json (that file stays the source; its notes and links sit behind the card's Sources toggle). Round 5: every wanted card (35 research entries and the three forecast-only home spots) is in this format; any entry without one is built from its fields in the same four parts (globe.js showCard).

nazare-praia-do-norte.question: Why do the biggest waves break here? The head of the Nazaré Canyon, a deep submarine canyon, comes close to the shore.
nazare-praia-do-norte.data: An open 25 m lidar grid of the coastal area (EMODnet, Instituto Hidrográfico, CC-BY 4.0).
nazare-praia-do-norte.shows: The coast and nearshore ground at 25 m spacing.
nazare-praia-do-norte.cant: Not fine enough for a reef-scale wave model, which needs seabed at about 10 m or finer. No such grid has been found yet.

funafuti-tuvalu.question: How do the reef edge and the 275 km² lagoon set wave exposure and flooding on an atoll whose land averages about two metres above the sea?
funafuti-tuvalu.data: No open seabed grid confirmed. Lagoon charts from a 2004 survey (1:20,000 to 1:50,000) are listed as open; a 2019 national lidar and bathymetry survey exists, but its public release is not confirmed.
funafuti-tuvalu.shows: The charts give lagoon depths at chart scale.
funafuti-tuvalu.cant: A chart scale is not a grid. Without seabed at about 10 m or finer there is no wave model here yet.

duck-frf-nc.question: How does a sandy beach change over decades? Profile lines round the Duck research pier have been surveyed since 1979.
duck-frf-nc.data: 28 profile lines about 45 m apart, ~600 m either side of the pier, 1979 to 2018 (PANGAEA, CC-BY 4.0), and a 2015 topobathy lidar point cloud (NOAA/USACE).
duck-frf-nc.shows: How the seabed along each line moved over nearly 40 years.
duck-frf-nc.cant: Lines are not a grid, and the lidar's resolution is not stated, so a 10 m seabed grid is not yet confirmed.

mavericks.question: Why do big winter swells rise so sharply here? A bedrock reef off Pillar Point makes them converge before they break, while typical northwest swells pass over gentler seabed.
mavericks.data: USGS California State Waters Map Series, Offshore of Half Moon Bay: multibeam bathymetry on a 2 m grid, mapped 2006-2007, from about the 10 m depth line outward. Public; no licence stated; not for navigation.
mavericks.shows: The reef and the seabed round it at 2 m, fine enough for a reef-scale wave model.
mavericks.cant: Water shallower than about 10 m may be missing, so the inner part of the break may not be in the grid.

teahupoo.question: How does the reef pass on Tahiti's southeast coast set where this wave breaks?
teahupoo.data: Shom's coastal topo-bathymetric model of Tahiti: about 20 m, lagoons to 100 m depth, Licence Ouverte 2.0, updated December 2023. Shom's Tahiti-Moorea model is about 100 m.
teahupoo.shows: The lagoon and coast of Tahiti at about 20 m, if the model reaches Teahupo'o.
teahupoo.cant: Its extent over Teahupo'o is not confirmed, and no 10 m product was found. The data status is not yet verified.

cloudbreak.question: How does the coral reef off Tavarua shape this left-hand wave in the Mamanuca group?
cloudbreak.data: Pacific Community (SPC) Digital Earth Pacific satellite-derived bathymetry: Sentinel-2, 10 m, CC BY 4.0, to about 30 m depth in clear water. The SOPAC Mamanuca chart (50 m) is restricted; the regional Fiji grid is about 300 m.
cloudbreak.shows: Seabed depths at 10 m in clear shallow water, if it covers the reef.
cloudbreak.cant: Coverage of Cloudbreak is not confirmed. Satellite-derived depths stop at about 30 m. The data status is not yet verified.

jaws-peahi.question: How do the reef and the offshore seabed off Pe'ahi, on Maui's north shore, shape this big-wave break?
jaws-peahi.data: NOAA NCEI Hawaii CUDEM: bathymetric-topographic tiles at 1/9 arc-second (about 3 m), published 2021, not subject to US copyright, not for navigation.
jaws-peahi.shows: Land and seabed round the main Hawaiian islands at about 3 m.
jaws-peahi.cant: The tile over Jaws has not been checked one by one, and the bathymetric accuracy is stated as variable.

skeleton-bay.question: How does a sand bank at Donkey Bay, on the Pelican Point spit, hold a left-hand wave said to run for up to about 2 km?
skeleton-bay.shows: Only where the spot is: the marker is the OpenStreetMap node "Donkey Bay", a point near the break, not the exact take-off.
skeleton-bay.cant: Without any seabed grid, nothing about the sand bank can be shown yet.

supertubes-jeffreys-bay.question: What shapes the long right-hand point wave at Jeffreys Bay?
supertubes-jeffreys-bay.shows: Only where the spot is (mapped in OpenStreetMap as a surfing spot).
supertubes-jeffreys-bay.cant: Without any seabed grid, nothing about the point can be shown yet. The data status is not yet verified.

cortes-bank.question: How does a seamount about 100 miles offshore, whose shallowest point (Bishop Rock) lies a few feet below the surface, focus swell?
cortes-bank.data: NCEI Coastal Relief Model, Southern California V2 (2013): 1 and 3 arc-second only (about 30 m or coarser). NOAA survey H04549 exists; its resolution is not stated.
cortes-bank.shows: The shape of the bank at about 30 m or coarser.
cortes-bank.cant: No 10 m grid is confirmed. The marker is the bank, not Bishop Rock itself. The data status is not yet verified.

mundaka.question: How does sand moving at the mouth of the Urdaibai estuary shape this left-hand wave?
mundaka.cant: Without any seabed grid, and with the sand moving, nothing about the break can be shown yet. The data status is not yet verified.

puerto-escondido-zicatela.question: How do offshore submarine canyons and shifting sand shape this heavy beach-break barrel on Oaxaca's coast?
puerto-escondido-zicatela.cant: Without any seabed grid, neither the canyons nor the sand can be shown yet. The data status is not yet verified.

uluwatu.question: How do reef shape and tide decide which section works below the cliff on Bali's Bukit Peninsula?
uluwatu.data: Indonesia's national bathymetry (BIG BATNAS): 6 arc-second (about 180 m), reported unreliable nearshore. No 10 m open data found.
uluwatu.shows: The broad seabed off Bali at about 180 m.
uluwatu.cant: Far too coarse for the reef. Digital Earth Pacific 10 m coverage of Bali is not confirmed. The data status is not yet verified.

bells-beach.question: How does the reef at this right-hand point break near Torquay, Victoria, shape the wave?
bells-beach.data: Victoria DEECA Victorian Coastal Digital Elevation Model 2021 (VCDEM): 10 m, CC BY 4.0. A 250 cm version also exists (CC BY 4.0).
bells-beach.shows: Coast and nearshore seabed at 10 m (and finer in the 250 cm version).
bells-beach.cant: The high-resolution version may have gaps, and how far offshore it reaches is not confirmed.

scripps-canyon-la-jolla.question: What does a narrow submarine canyon, about 1.6 km long and 490 m deep off La Jolla, do to the waves above it?
scripps-canyon-la-jolla.data: USGS SIM 3324 (Scripps 2013 multibeam): public, but down-sampled to 25 m. CSUMB mapped the canyon head by multibeam in October 2001, resolution not stated, available on request, not as a download.
scripps-canyon-la-jolla.cant: 25 m is too coarse for the break, and the finer canyon-head survey is not openly downloadable. The data status is not yet verified.

monterey-canyon-moss-landing.question: How does the head of the largest submarine canyon on the North American west coast, starting near Moss Landing, meet the shore?
monterey-canyon-moss-landing.data: MBARI AUV 1 m grids (MGDS, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), only for 200-500 m and 1,350-1,880 m depths. Ship multibeam from 1998 as raw files at NOAA NGDC; a Stanford compilation is for affiliates only.
monterey-canyon-moss-landing.shows: Parts of the deep canyon at 1 m.
monterey-canyon-moss-landing.cant: Not the shallow canyon head near shore, which is what a wave model needs. The marker is the marine lab; the canyon head is just offshore.

narrabeen-collaroy-sydney.question: How does a 3.6 km beach change month by month? Five sites have been surveyed every month since April 1976.
narrabeen-collaroy-sydney.data: Open profile data (CC-BY 4.0 paper, live repository at narrabeen.wrl.unsw.edu.au): five transects to 20 m depth, plus airborne lidar since 2011.
narrabeen-collaroy-sydney.shows: How the beach and nearshore along five lines changed over nearly 50 years.
narrabeen-collaroy-sydney.cant: Lines are not a grid: a gridded open seabed at 10 m or finer is not confirmed, and the licence listings on data.gov.au disagree.

truc-vert-aquitaine.question: How does a remote, never-nourished, high-energy sandy beach change? Sixteen years of topographic surveys are open data.
truc-vert-aquitaine.data: Shom/IGN Litto3D Nouvelle-Aquitaine 2020-2022: airborne lidar, "metric resolution", to about 20 m depth, Etalab 2.0 open licence, not for navigation. Beach survey DEMs on OSF, CC-BY 4.0.
truc-vert-aquitaine.shows: Beach and nearshore seabed at about metre scale, to about 20 m depth.
truc-vert-aquitaine.cant: The exact grid size is not stated on the record, and it is a single 2020-2022 survey.

egmond-aan-zee.question: What can the Dutch national seabed grid show of the nearshore off a North Sea beach town?
egmond-aan-zee.data: Rijkswaterstaat Bathymetrie Nederland (coast and vaklodingen): 20 m grid, CC0 1.0.
egmond-aan-zee.cant: 20 m is coarser than the 10 m a wave model needs, and no finer public grid for Egmond is confirmed. The data status is not yet verified.

perranporth-cornwall.question: How does a dissipative, macrotidal sandy beach respond to waves? Surveys and wave forcing are published for 2006 to 2021.
perranporth-cornwall.data: A merged lidar and multibeam DEM on a 2 m grid (McCarroll et al., Scientific Data 2023, CC-BY 4.0, hosted by the University of Plymouth). Environment Agency lidar via the Plymouth Coastal Observatory.
perranporth-cornwall.shows: Beach and nearshore seabed at 2 m.
perranporth-cornwall.cant: Exact coverage of the break is not yet confirmed.

heron-island-gbr.question: How do waves cross a coral reef flat to a cay in the southern Great Barrier Reef?
heron-island-gbr.data: Heron Reef 1 m bathymetry from airborne hyperspectral data (CASI, July 2002), CC BY 3.0, on PANGAEA. Geoscience Australia multibeam at 2 m to 64 m (CC-BY 4.0).
heron-island-gbr.cant: The 1 m depths are not tide-corrected and have gaps; whether the multibeam actually covers the island is unconfirmed.

raglan-manu-bay.question: How do the three left-hand point breaks near Raglan (Manu Bay, Whale Bay, Indicators) wrap along the coast?
raglan-manu-bay.data: LINZ national coastal DEM: 1 m tiles from lidar to about 25 m depth, CC-BY 4.0, on AWS Open Data. A Waikato regional report has 50 m grids only.
raglan-manu-bay.shows: Coast and nearshore seabed at 1 m, where the lidar reaches.
raglan-manu-bay.cant: Coverage of the Raglan coast is not confirmed.

kirra-superbank-gold-coast.question: How has pumping sand across the Tweed River mouth since 2001 reshaped Kirra Point, where barrels once broke?
kirra-superbank-gold-coast.data: None found as a grid. Tweed Sand Bypassing reports show 1997 and 2011 bathymetry only as figures.
kirra-superbank-gold-coast.cant: No downloadable grid was located, so the change cannot be shown. The data status is not yet verified.

hulhumale-maldives.question: How exposed is a reclaimed island? Hulhumalé, home to 65,714 people (2022 census), was built by pumping sand from the sea floor beside Malé.
hulhumale-maldives.data: None confirmed. A 2021 Maldives-wide gridded bathymetry paper exists (doi 10.1029/2020EA001207).
hulhumale-maldives.cant: Its resolution near Malé and its licence are unconfirmed, so no wave exposure can be shown. The data status is not yet verified.

happisburgh-norfolk-uk.question: Why do these soft glacial-till cliffs retreat so fast? About 20 m was lost in 2004-2007.
happisburgh-norfolk-uk.data: Environment Agency SurfZone DEM, 2 m (lidar plus nearshore multibeam, Open Government Licence, covers 50-55.8° N). The EA lidar composite DTM at 1 m is land only.
happisburgh-norfolk-uk.shows: Cliffs and beach at 1-2 m; nearshore seabed at 2 m where the SurfZone DEM has it.
happisburgh-norfolk-uk.cant: Whether the SurfZone DEM holds seabed off Happisburgh is unverified.

grand-isle-louisiana-usa.question: How does a barrier island at the mouth of Barataria Bay buffer inland parishes from hurricane surge and waves?
grand-isle-louisiana-usa.data: NOAA NCEI Southern Louisiana Coastal DEM at 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m), not subject to US copyright, not for navigation. CUDEM 1/9 arc-second (about 3 m) tiles also exist.
grand-isle-louisiana-usa.shows: Island, bay and nearshore seabed at about 10 m.
grand-isle-louisiana-usa.cant: Whether a 3 m CUDEM tile covers Grand Isle is not confirmed tile by tile.

sendai-bay-japan.question: How does the seabed of Sendai Bay, on the Miyagi coast, shape tsunami inundation?
sendai-bay-japan.data: NIED Global tsunami Terrain Model: whole-Japan grid at two arc-seconds (about 50 m), CC BY 4.0, with 2016 Cabinet Office nesting data in the Japan Trench area. Finer Japan Hydrographic Association grids appear to be sold.
sendai-bay-japan.shows: The bay's seabed at about 50 m.
sendai-bay-japan.cant: No grid at 10 m or finer was found, and Sendai Bay coverage is not explicitly stated. The data status is not yet verified.

banda-aceh-indonesia.question: How did the coast of the closest major city to the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake (about 249 km away) take the tsunami, and how has it recovered?
banda-aceh-indonesia.data: None found at 10 m or finer. Indonesia's national bathymetry (BIG BATNAS) is listed at 6 arc-seconds (about 180 m).
banda-aceh-indonesia.shows: Nothing at reef or beach scale.
banda-aceh-indonesia.cant: Public download of BATNAS is not confirmed, and the national bathymetry system is reported as restricted to government institutions. The data status is not yet verified.

hilo-bay-hawaii-usa.question: How does Hilo Bay, behind its 1908-1929 breakwater, flood in a tsunami, as it did in 1946 and 1960?
hilo-bay-hawaii-usa.data: NOAA NCEI Hilo, Hawaii integrated bathymetric-topographic DEM at 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m), built for tsunami forecasting, CC0 1.0 per its catalogue record.
hilo-bay-hawaii-usa.shows: Bay, breakwater and town at about 10 m.
hilo-bay-hawaii-usa.cant: The record's details are inconsistent (location box and access level), so access is not yet confirmed.

venice-lagoon-inlets-italy.question: What did the lagoon's inlets and channels look like before the MOSE flood barriers began to operate? They were mapped in 2013.
venice-lagoon-inlets-italy.data: EMODnet "Venice Lagoon Channels DTM 5 m" (CNR-ISMAR, 2013 multibeam, CC BY 4.0, not for navigation). The source paper reports 0.5 m bathymetry on MGDS.
venice-lagoon-inlets-italy.shows: Inlet and channel seabed at 5 m, a before-baseline.
venice-lagoon-inlets-italy.cant: One 2013 snapshot. The 0.5 m dataset's licence is not stated. The seabed is in hand; the swell model is the next step, not done yet.

coxs-bazar-bangladesh.question: How do cyclone surge and waves drive flood risk for about 196,000 residents on a floodplain lower than the dunes?
coxs-bazar-bangladesh.data: None found. A Cox's Bazar storm-surge study used bathymetry from local agencies that is not public.
coxs-bazar-bangladesh.cant: Without open seabed data, surge and waves cannot be shown. The data status is not yet verified.

drew-point-alaska-usa.question: Why does this permafrost bluff coast erode by up to 20 m a year, as USGS cites? Storms cut niches into the bluffs.
drew-point-alaska-usa.data: None found for Drew Point. USGS has flown airborne lidar of the north coast (topography; release not named). A 2022 USGS single-beam nearshore survey exists at Point Barrow, about 100 km west.
drew-point-alaska-usa.shows: Nothing here yet; the nearest survey is 100 km away.
drew-point-alaska-usa.cant: No nearshore seabed at Drew Point, so the storm waves at the bluff cannot be modelled.

galveston-island-texas-usa.question: How does a Gulf barrier island behind a seawall and raised grade (built after the 1900 hurricane surge) meet surge and waves today?
galveston-island-texas-usa.data: NOAA NCEI Galveston, Texas Coastal DEM: 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) to 3 arc-second, CC0 1.0 per its catalogue, published 2007. CUDEM 1/9 arc-second (about 3 m) tiles also cover the contiguous US.
galveston-island-texas-usa.shows: Island and nearshore seabed at about 10 m.
galveston-island-texas-usa.cant: The 2007 DEM may be dated, and tile-by-tile CUDEM coverage is not checked.

lagos-victoria-island-nigeria.question: How does erosion work on this wave-dominated barrier coast, where the Eko Atlantic development is built on reclaimed land next door?
lagos-victoria-island-nigeria.data: None found. A local 1 m topo-bathymetric survey at Maiyegun Estate is listed in a catalogue. GEBCO (about 450 m) is too coarse.
lagos-victoria-island-nigeria.cant: The 1 m survey's access terms are unknown, so no seabed can be shown. The data status is not yet verified.

majuro-marshall-islands.question: How do reef, lagoon and wave exposure shape flooding on an atoll of 23,156 people whose highest point is under 3 m?
majuro-marshall-islands.data: Listed but not yet confirmed: a USGS 1 m topobathymetric DEM of Majuro Atoll (DOI 10.5066/F7416VXX; 1944-2016 data; satellite-derived nearshore depths, RMSE about 1.1 m) and an SPC/GEM 5 m lagoon bathymetry DEM.
majuro-marshall-islands.shows: Atoll, reef and lagoon at 1-5 m, if confirmed.
majuro-marshall-islands.cant: Neither dataset nor its licence is confirmed yet. The data status is not yet verified.

klitmoller.question: Klitmøller breaks over a reef: what does that reef do to the swell?
klitmoller.shows: The spot is marked; there is no model yet.
klitmoller.cant: Needed: a seabed depth survey of the Klitmøller reef at 10 m resolution or finer.

hvide_sande.question: How do the moving sandbars at Hvide Sande shape the waves?
hvide_sande.shows: The spot is marked; there is no model yet.
hvide_sande.cant: Needed: a recent seabed depth survey of the sandbars at 10 m resolution or finer. Bars move, so any survey ages.

tel_aviv.question: What does the seabed of the Tel Aviv surf zone do to the swell?
tel_aviv.shows: The spot is marked; there is no model yet.
tel_aviv.cant: Needed: a seabed depth survey of the Tel Aviv surf zone at 10 m resolution or finer.
